title: Converting between metric and US customary
blurb: Cross between the two systems with unit fractions: inches and centimeters, pounds and kilograms, and any factor the question gives you.
question: A child weighs 44 lb, and a medication is ordered at 15 mg per kilogram per day, split into 3 equal doses. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how many milligrams are in each dose?

teach.h: A bridge factor joins the two systems
teach.body: Formally, a conversion factor is a ratio of two equal quantities in different units, such as 1 in = 2.54 cm; multiplying by it changes the unit but not the amount. In plain English: one fact links a customary unit to a metric one, and you multiply or divide by that fact. A few bridge facts are expected from memory. Any other factor the TEAS needs will be printed in the question, so use exactly the number it gives you.

teach.caption: Because 1 ft = 12 in, 1 ft = 12 × 2.54 = 30.48 cm. Build other length facts the same way.

teach.h: Unit fractions: let the units decide
teach.body: Write the bridge fact as a fraction with the unit you WANT on top and the unit you are getting rid of on the bottom, then multiply. The unwanted unit cancels. 66 in × (2.54 cm / 1 in) = 167.64 cm. 154 lb × (1 kg / 2.2 lb) = 70 kg. If the units do not cancel, the fraction is upside down, and you would be multiplying when you should divide.

teach.caption: Chain several fractions in a row for multi-step problems (lb to kg, then kg to mg of dose).

rows.label: Why
values: A kg is the heavier unit
A lb is the lighter unit

teach.caption: Sense check: a person's weight in kilograms is always a smaller number than in pounds.

items: 10 km to miles, using 1 mi = 1.6 km: 10 ÷ 1.6 = 6.25 mi. Check: 6.25 × 1.6 = 10 km.
2 L to quarts, using 1 L = 1.06 qt: 2 × 1.06 = 2.12 qt. Check: 2.12 ÷ 1.06 = 2 L.

teach.caption: A meter is a little longer than a yard (1 yd = 0.9144 m exactly).

teach.h: Scenario: Priya checks a weight-based dose
teach.body: Priya, a CNA preparing for the TEAS, sees a patient weighing 132 lb with an order for 2 mg of a drug per kilogram. Step 1, pounds to kilograms: 132 ÷ 2.2 = 60 kg. Step 2, the dose: 60 × 2 = 120 mg. Check: 60 × 2.2 = 132 lb. If she had multiplied by 2.2 instead, she would have used 290.4 kg and calculated a dose nearly five times too large.

teach.text: Multiply or divide? lb to kg is DIVIDE by 2.2; kg to lb is MULTIPLY. in to cm is MULTIPLY by 2.54; cm to in is DIVIDE. Also watch for 2.54 used on feet (convert feet to inches first) and weight ounces mixed up with fluid ounces (28 g vs 30 mL).

items: Memorize: 1 in = 2.54 cm; 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb; 1 tsp = 5 mL; 1 tbsp = 15 mL; 1 fl oz ≈ 30 mL.
Other factors (mi/km, L/qt, oz/g, gal/L) come in the question: use them exactly.
Write the factor with the wanted unit on top so the old unit cancels.
Convert mixed units first (5 ft 6 in = 66 in), then cross systems.
Sense check every answer: kg is less than lb; cm is more than in.

summary: You can now cross between metric and US customary units using the memorized bridge facts or a factor given in the question. You set each factor up as a unit fraction, so you always know whether to multiply or divide, and you can chain steps for weight-based doses.

A.q: A patient weighs 187 lb. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the patient's weight in kilograms?
A.why: Pounds to kilograms: divide by 2.2. 187 ÷ 2.2 = 85 kg. Check: 85 × 2.2 = 187 lb.

whyNot.0: This multiplies by 2.2. A weight in kilograms must be a smaller number than in pounds.
whyNot.3: The division is right but the decimal point has slipped one place.

A.q: A wound measures 3.5 in long. What is its length in centimeters, to the nearest hundredth?

whyNot.0: This divides by 2.54. Centimeters are smaller than inches, so the number must get bigger.
whyNot.1: The decimal point has slipped one place to the right.
whyNot.2: This rounds the factor to 2.5; the exact factor is 2.54.

A.q: Using 1 mile = 1.6 kilometers, how many miles long is a 10 km charity run?
A.why: Kilometers to miles: 10 km × (1 mi / 1.6 km) = 10 ÷ 1.6 = 6.25 mi. Check: 6.25 × 1.6 = 10 km.

whyNot.1: This multiplies by 1.6. A mile is longer than a kilometer, so there are fewer miles than kilometers.
whyNot.2: This subtracts 1.6 instead of dividing by it.
whyNot.3: The division is right but the decimal point has slipped one place.

B.q: A baby weighs 4.5 kg. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, what is the baby's weight in pounds and ounces, to the nearest ounce?
B.why: 4.5 × 2.2 = 9.9 lb. Keep 9 lb and convert the 0.9 lb: 0.9 × 16 = 14.4, which rounds to 14 oz. So 9 lb 14 oz.

whyNot.0: This reads 0.9 lb as 9 oz. A pound has 16 ounces, so 0.9 lb is 14.4 oz.
whyNot.1: This divides by 2.2 (4.5 ÷ 2.2 is about 2.05 lb). kg to lb means multiply.
whyNot.3: This uses 12 oz per pound (0.9 × 12 = 10.8, about 11 oz).

B.q: Using 1 L = 1.06 qt, about how many quarts does a 2-liter bottle hold, to the nearest hundredth?
B.why: Liters to quarts: 2 L × (1.06 qt / 1 L) = 2.12 qt. Check: 2.12 ÷ 1.06 = 2 L.

whyNot.0: This divides by 1.06; the factor is written with quarts on top, so multiply.
whyNot.2: This adds 1.06 to 2 instead of multiplying.

B.q: A nursing applicant is 5 ft 4 in tall. What is this height in centimeters, to the nearest hundredth?

whyNot.0: This reads 5 ft 4 in as 54 in (54 × 2.54 = 137.16).
whyNot.1: This reads 5 ft 4 in as 5.4 ft (64.8 in), but 4 in is 4/12 of a foot, not 0.4.
whyNot.2: This divides 64 by 2.54 instead of multiplying.

C.q: A child weighs 44 lb. A medication is ordered at 15 mg per kg per day, split into 3 equal doses. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how many milligrams are in each dose?

whyNot.1: 300 mg is the daily total; the question asks for one of the 3 doses.
whyNot.2: This skips the conversion and uses 44 lb as if it were kilograms (44 × 15 ÷ 3).
whyNot.3: This multiplies 44 by 2.2 (96.8 kg), the wrong direction.

C.q: Using 1 gallon = 3.785 liters, how many liters does a 15-gallon water tank hold, to the nearest tenth?
C.why: 15 × 3.785 = 56.775 L. The hundredths digit is 7, so round up: 56.8 L.

whyNot.0: This divides 15 by 3.785. Liters are smaller than gallons, so the number must get bigger.
whyNot.1: This truncates 56.775 instead of rounding; a 7 in the hundredths place rounds the tenths up.
whyNot.3: This adds 3.785 to 15 instead of multiplying.

C.q: Jordan walks 2.4 km to a clinic and returns 1.5 mi by a different route. Using 1 mile = 1.6 km, what is the total distance in miles, to the nearest tenth?

whyNot.0: This multiplies 2.4 by 1.6 (3.84) instead of dividing, then adds 1.5.
whyNot.2: This adds 2.4 and 1.5 without converting the kilometers.
whyNot.3: 4.8 is the total in kilometers, not miles.

reteach.title: Think of exchanging currency
reteach.question: Changing dollars into another currency uses an exchange rate. How is a bridge factor like an exchange rate?

blocks.body: At a currency desk, the rate tells you how many units of one currency equal one unit of the other. Changing money does not change its value, only the label and the number. A conversion factor is an exchange rate for units: 1 in "buys" 2.54 cm, and 1 kg "buys" 2.2 lb. When you exchange into the smaller unit, you receive more of them; into the bigger unit, fewer.

blocks.text: Before you calculate, decide whether you should end up with more units or fewer. If your answer goes the other way, you multiplied when you should have divided.

explain.body: 1 in = 2.54 cm exactly, so 1 ft = 12 × 2.54 = 30.48 cm. 1 kg ≈ 2.2 lb is the standard health-care factor.

test.q: How many centimeters are in 1 foot?

whyNot.0: 2.54 cm is one inch, not one foot.
whyNot.1: This divides 12 by 2.54 instead of multiplying.
whyNot.3: 25.4 is the number of millimeters in one inch.

explain.body: Put the unit you want on top. To turn kg into lb, multiply by (2.2 lb / 1 kg) so that kg cancels.

test.q: Which setup correctly converts 68 kg to pounds?
test.why: With pounds on top and kilograms on the bottom, kg cancels and the answer is in pounds: 68 × 2.2 = 149.6 lb.

whyNot.1: Kilograms are on top, so nothing cancels: this divides by 2.2.
whyNot.2: Dividing by the fraction is the same as dividing by 2.2, the wrong direction.
whyNot.3: This factor is false: 1 lb is not equal to 2.2 kg.

explain.body: For miles, quarts, weight ounces and gallons the TEAS gives the factor. Use that exact number, and keep weight ounces (28 g) apart from fluid ounces (30 mL).

test.q: Using 1 oz = 28 g, about how many ounces is a 340 g package of pasta, to the nearest tenth?
test.why: Grams to ounces: 340 ÷ 28 = 12.14..., which rounds to 12.1 oz.

whyNot.1: This divides by 16, the ounces-per-pound factor, which does not convert grams.
whyNot.2: This divides by 30, the fluid-ounce factor for milliliters; weight ounces use 28 g.

explain.body: Turn mixed customary units into one unit before crossing systems: 1 ft 8 in = 12 + 8 = 20 in, then 20 × 2.54 = 50.8 cm.

test.q: A newborn is 1 ft 8 in long. What is the length in centimeters, to the nearest tenth?

whyNot.0: This reads 1 ft 8 in as 1.8 ft; 8 in is 8/12 of a foot.
whyNot.2: This converts the foot (30.48 cm) but adds the 8 in without converting them.
whyNot.3: This divides 20 by 2.54 instead of multiplying.
